Careers Summer Camp Guide: STEM Summer Camps Metro Creative ServicesMetro ServicesA roundup of STEM summer camps in Asheville and Western North Carolina, including locations, dates, and links to information and registration. STEM camps are built for curious kids who like to learn by doing, with hands-on programs focused on science, technology, engineering, math, coding, robotics, and creative problem-solving. Below is a roundup of STEM summer camps in Asheville and across Western North Carolina, including each camp’s location, session dates, and a link to details or registration. Camps often add sessions as summer gets closer, so this list is updated as new information is announced. Back to the full 2026 Summer Camp Guide Asheville Math 856 Sweeten Creek Road, Asheville NC 28803 | 828-367-3269 Asheville Math runs imaginative, hands‑on summer camps where kids explore math through creative projects, puzzles, and build‑it challenges. Camps include activities like cracking codes, making origami, engineering balloon‑drop devices, designing optical art, and playing strategy‑based games. Young Minds Math Camp | July 6-10 Games Math Camp | July 13-17 Asheville Museum of Science 43 Patton Ave, Asheville, NC 28801 | 828-254-7162 Programming contributes to campers’ interest in and understanding of concepts ranging from exploring our natural world, and computer programming to chemistry. June 15-19 | Paleontology and Archaeology: Campers will explore fossils and evidence of the past with hands-on activities. June 22-26 | Tinkering Workshop: Campers will be introduced to the use of tools and materials with imaginative prompts. June 29 – July 3 | Space Explorers: Campers will explore outer space! July 6-10 | The Natural World: From animals and plants to rocks and volcanos, campers will be July 13-17 | The Art of Science: Campers will be amazed at the ways science and art are interconnected! July 20-24 | Chemistry: Campers will experiment with everyday chemicals to explore concepts like pH, capillary action, and chemical reactions. July 27 – July 31 | Forces and Energy: Campers have fun with physics concepts to make things drop, stop and roll! August 3 – 7 | The Art of Science II: Campers will continue to be amazed at the ways science and art are interconnected! Camp Invention 74 Riverwood Road, Swannanoa, NC 28778 | 828-581-2200 A fun, hands‑on STEM camp where kids spend the week building simple inventions, exploring creative challenges, and learning how ideas come to life through experimentation and teamwork. June 8-12 COMPASS at Montreat College 310 Gaither Circle, Montreat, NC 28757 | 828-669-8012 COMPASS is a week‑long summer immersion program designed for rising high school sophomores through rising college freshmen who want a hands‑on introduction to potential academic and career paths. Courses available include Psychology, Audio Production, Criminal Justice, Cybersecurity, Exercise Science, Herpetology, Literature & Creative Writing, Graphic Design, Outdoor Recreation Studies, History (Heroes, and Heretics) and Apologetics (LOL-ogetics) June 21-25 The Educational Garden Project 15 Overbrook Place, Asheville, NC 28805 | 828-989-9647 A hands‑on garden program where kids learn by planting, tending, and harvesting, discovering how food grows while exploring nature through simple, interactive outdoor activities. Baby Animals | June 8-12 Bees + Bugs | June 15-19 Birds | June 22-26 Herbal remedies | June 29-July 3 Wild Animals of Appalachia | July 6-10 Outdoor Skills and Tools | July 13-17 Trees | July 20-25 Flowers | July 27-31 Fungi | August 3-7 Butterflies | August 10-14 Farm Animals | August 17-21 Forest Floor 315 Old Haw Creek Rd, Asheville, NC 28805 | 828-338-9787 A nature‑immersive camp where kids spend their days exploring the woods, learning through hands‑on play, and connecting with the rhythms of the forest through stories, crafts, and outdoor skills. Weekly Camps | June 8-August 14 Hands On! Children’s Museum 318 North Main Street, Hendersonville, NC 28792 | 828-697-8333 A full‑day, activity‑packed camp where rising 1st–3rd graders dive into hands‑on science, creative projects, and themed learning led by museum educators. Kids explore experiments, build, imagine, and problem‑solve through interactive stations and guided activities designed to spark curiosity.
